name: RoboBench
description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation across five dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. It spans 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
citeAs: Luo, Yulin et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations, with customized workflows for each dimension. Instruction comprehension uses paired explicit and implicit instructions, where implicit instructions are rewritten from explicit ones using LLMs. Perception reasoning uses real robot data with type and view metadata, curated static attributes, GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning is built from high-quality robotic videos, extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs. Affordance prediction samples representative frames from the planning pool and annotates static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis collects execution-level failures from RoboMIND and synthesizes planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source and in-house robotic data; large-scale real-world robotic datasets; high-quality robotic videos; real robot data with type and view metadata; execution-level failures from RoboMIND.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Implicit instructions are obtained by rewriting explicit instructions into demand-based requests using LLMs. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions with wrong object, missing step, and wrong order. Each planning step is mapped into function templates grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The construction pipeline generally follows preprocessing, annotation with VLMs, detection models or human experts, and Q&A format generation. Frame sequences are extracted from robotic videos as standardized inputs. Data are standardized into multiple-choice QA for perception tasks. General and task-specific filters are applied during construction, addressing image quality and task validity, such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators inspect linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is used: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail undergo manual review and correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are produced by both models and humans. Gemini generates structured annotations for planning data, including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata such as objects, actions, scenes, and embodiments; these are refined by human annotators. Perception reasoning uses template-based QA, GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Affordance prediction annotates representative frames with static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile base positions. Execution-level failures are labeled by experts. Human evaluators also validate benchmark quality for linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A two-stage quality control process is used: filtering during construction and post-construction validation. After data construction, 20 professionally trained annotators conduct comprehensive quality inspections. A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators; expert annotators with prior training; execution-level failures labeled by experts.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLMs, MLLMs, VLMs, detection models, GPT, Gemini
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench is intended to provide a unified scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which the authors attribute as a reason for failures in dual-arm coordination and mobile manipulation. It also notes that models perform relatively better on common, well-seen objects than on uncommon objects, symbolic reasoning, or world knowledge tasks.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark lacks real-world planning failure data, so planning-level failures are synthesized. Human performance on execution-level failure diagnosis is relatively low, underscoring the intrinsic difficulty of the task. The paper also reports that current MLLMs exhibit only superficial embodied reasoning and world-modeling capabilities, with major gaps in implicit instruction grounding, spatiotemporal reasoning, cross-scenario planning, fine-grained affordance understanding, and execution failure diagnosis.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It is used for evaluation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis, including long-horizon planning, next-step planning, task state estimation, multiple-choice QA, and point or trajectory prediction.
